newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GRAINS SURGE KEEPS HUNGARY FX FUTURES TRADE LOW.
newsitem.headline: GRAINS SURGE KEEPS HUNGARY FX FUTURES TRADE LOW.

text.p: Soaring prices on the grains futures market and a surging dollar/mark kept trade low on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE), dealers said.
The BCE saw turnover of just 795 million forints after registering no more than 1.6 billion on the previous three trading days.

Hungary's milling wheat futures prices continued to soar on Wednesday motored by concerns over the quality of the crop and expectations of a rise in demand in Poland due to floods there, traders said.
Grains turnover rocketed to the highest daily figure this year with 1.668 billion forints, up from Tuesday's one billion forints.
On the BCE forex futures market the mark fell for all maturities while the the dollar rose for all months by between 1.6 and four forints.
Turnover on the smaller Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) once again outpaced the BCE, totalling 2.9 billion forints, most of which was taken up two dollar/mark basket deals for December.

Basket deals, by which dollars and marks are traded in the 30/70 proportion they represent in the central bank's currency basket against which the forint floats, are seen as a way of hedging against large dollar/mark fluctuations.

The December mark fell 0.65 to 113.05 forints while the December dollar rose 1.75 to 205. The dollar also rose on the BSE for August, September and next March by 3.37, 1.95 and 2.80 fornts respectively.
